端到端自动化:研究→生成→优化(实时 SEO 评分)→直发 CMS→按 3-180 天随机排期自动上线

verifications.claim: Byword pricing: monthly $99/$299/$999 = 25/80/300 articles; annual $83/$249/$833 (save 17%); 5 free articles no credit card; overage $2.50-$3.50/article; Unlimited tier form disputed by third parties ($1,999 vs $2,499 vs $0 BYO-key).
verifications.evidence:
Verified against the live, JS-rendered first-party byword.ai/pricing page (WebFetch could not read it — site is client-rendered — so I used a headless browser and read document.body.innerText for both toggle states). EXACT renders:
- Monthly toggle: Starter $99/mo = 25 articles/mo, $3.50 per extra article, 5 domains, solo; Standard $299/mo = 80 articles/mo, $3.00 per extra, 3 seats (+$25/extra), unlimited domains, API access; Scale $999/mo = 300 articles/mo, $2.50 per extra, 10 seats (+$20/extra), unlimited domains, priority support.
- Annual toggle (this is the page DEFAULT view): $83 / $249 / $833 per mo with banner "Save 17% with annual billing" and "Save $198/$598/$1,998 /yr". So both the monthly numbers, the annual numbers, AND the exact 17% all confirm verbatim.
- Free trial: "Every account starts with 5 free articles. No credit card required." Confirmed verbatim.
- Overage range $2.50–$3.50 confirmed (Free credit price $5.00; Starter $3.50; Standard $3.00; Scale $2.50). The FAQ also states "articles cost between $2.50 and $3.50 each."
The ONE genuinely unresolved element is the Unlimited tier's CURRENT FORM — and the dispute is real because Byword's OWN two pages conflict right now: (1) byword.ai/pricing renders Unlimited as "$0 PLATFORM / MONTH, ~$0.00 per article (avg), infinite team seats, 'Your keys. Our platform.'" = a BYO-API-key model with $0 platform fee; (2) the official docs byword.ai/learn/docs/account/billing lists "Unlimited $1,999/mo, Unlimited credits/seats/domains." The third-party $2,499 figure (from search snippets/SEOmatic-style comparison pages) is NOT corroborated by any current first-party page and appears stale. Net: the precise, load-bearing tiered numbers and structure are confirmed exactly as stated; for Unlimited, the live first-party reality is two coexisting forms ($0 BYO-key on /pricing and $1,999/mo in docs), with $2,499 uncorroborated — consistent with the claim's own caveat that Unlimited needs per-form verification.

verifications.claim: Byword currently has NO built-in plagiarism detection, fact-checking, humanizer, or true deduplication — it only uses "one article per keyword" positioning, making "no quality control" a safe core attack point.
verifications.evidence:
The simplistic attack framing ("they have none / don't even claim it") is UNSAFE — refuted by Byword's own first-party sources. Byword's official changelog (v2.0.0 "The Relaunch", Jan 19 2026, https://byword.ai/changelog) explicitly lists as shipped: "Fact-checking mode with source citations and verification", "Plagiarism-free guarantee with originality verification", and (under Improved) "More natural, human-like writing that passes AI detection." Byword also hosts standalone tools at byword.ai/tools/humanizer, /tools/ai-content-detector, and /tools/paragraph-rewriter (confirmed in its tools sitemap). A March 31 2026 hands-on review states "Byword includes a feature to help its output evade detection." This is exactly the "recent stealth launch" risk the question warned about: do NOT claim Byword has zero quality-check messaging.

BUT the deeper substantive claim (these features are real/working) is largely supported by functional evidence: (1) Byword's own detailed product docs describe the generation pipeline as only Research -> Outline -> Content Generation -> Enhancement (internal links, meta, images, table of contents) with NO fact-check/plagiarism/originality/humanizer/dedup step (https://byword.ai/learn/docs/content/articles); the dedicated AI Generation feature page omits them too; and the full /learn docs sitemap contains NO page for plagiarism, fact-checking, originality, humanizer, or deduplication. (2) Three independent 2026 hands-on reviews find no functioning built-in plagiarism checker or fact-checker and report unedited Byword output scores 85-95% AI on Originality.ai (aboahreviews Mar 31 2026), with human editing required before publishing (originality.ai Aug 2025; aitoolshop Apr 30 2026). Notably, deduplication/uniqueness-across-pages (the user's actual moat) is NOT addressed by any Byword feature or claim.

Net: the changelog/marketing CLAIMS fact-check + originality verification + a humanizer (and the humanizer/AI-detector tools genuinely exist as standalone utilities), but the functional docs + independent tests show no substantive in-pipeline plagiarism/fact-check step and a humanizer that does not reliably pass AI detection. Hence uncertain, not confirmed. Caveat: I could not log into the product to test the in-app "fact-checking mode" toggle directly, and the live browser session intermittently mis-navigated to other sites, so the changelog claim could not be independently confirmed/disconfirmed inside the app. Recommendation: reframe the attack point away from "they have no quality control" toward "Byword's plagiarism/fact-check claims are unverified marketing with no docs and failing independent AI-detection tests, and they have NO cross-page deduplication — our deterministic dedup/uniqueness engine is the real, verifiable moat."

verifications.claim: Byword 的 AI 可检测性数据"未编辑 85-95% AI 概率(Originality.ai)、需重写才降<30%"来自单一 30 天评测,应独立复测验证量级。
verifications.evidence:
该论断的"来源属性"经证伪式核查后成立。这组精确数字唯一可追溯到单篇博客:aboahreviews.com《Byword AI Review 2026: I Tested This SEO Content Generation Tool for 30 Days》(作者 Aboah Okyere,2026-03-31 发布)。原文逐字写道:"unedited Byword articles scored 85% to 95% AI probability on Originality AI";"After my standard editing pass, that dropped to 40% to 60%. Heavy rewriting brought it below 30%"——与论断中的量级与措辞几乎完全一致,确证其确实出自单一 30 天评测。

证据强度三点:(1) 单一来源、无独立复现:对该精确数字(85-95% / 40-60% / <30%)的所有检索变体只命中这一篇 aboahreviews 文章;未找到任何第三方独立复测得出同等数字。(2) 第一方仅证"会被检出"、不证量级:Originality.ai 官方的 Byword 评测页(originality.ai/blog/byword-ai-review)确认 Byword 内容会被其检出("Of course it does"),但全文无任何百分比、无 30 天框架、无 "<30%" 阈值——即官方并不背书这组数字。(3) 方法学薄弱:该评测为单人叙述,30 天内跨 3 个 niche 共生成约 47 篇文章,但 AI 检测一节为纯文字叙述——无截图、无数据表、无逐篇分数、未说明检测样本数;站点无透明 affiliate 披露且带营销 CTA,属典型单博主 SEO 推广向评测,不可复现。

结论:论断主张的"单一 30 天评测来源 + 该量级"属实,故 confirmed。论断同时建议的"自行用 Byword 试用额度生成→过 Originality/GPTZero 独立复测"这一动作我在本环境无法执行(无 Byword 试用账号与检测器访问),因此该独立复测建议仍然成立且尚未被任何公开第一手实验满足——这恰恰加强而非削弱了论断的合理性。

verifications.claim: KoalaWriter (Koala AI) has two real, representative soft spots: (1) users' entire sites get banned by Google, and (2) Originality.ai flags its output 100% AI — and the question is whether these are isolated anecdotes or a general phenomenon (SearchLogistics methodology/sample/date; whether Koala has improved).
verifications.evidence:
Both data points exist in primary sources but are materially misrepresented as Koala-specific, representative weaknesses; the truth is more nuanced.

(A) "Originality.ai 100% AI on Koala" — TRUE BUT NOT KOALA-SPECIFIC. Primary source is the SearchLogistics AI Content Detection case study (searchlogistics.com/learn/tools/ai-content-detection-case-study/). Methodology: 14 AI writing tools x 5 articles = 60 pieces, run through 11 detectors; originally Jan 2023, updated May 20 2026. Originality.ai scored 100% AI on Koala.sh — but ALSO 100% on ChatGPT 4o, Claude Sonnet, Jasper, Writesonic and effectively all 14 tools (it was "the only tool to hit ~100% detection across all 14"). Crucially, the same study's human-written control articles were flagged at ~27% AI by Originality.ai (false positives). So the 100% reflects Originality.ai's aggressiveness, not a unique Koala flaw — any AI writer (and even humans, partially) gets flagged. Using it as a Koala-specific weakness is misleading.

(B) "Entire sites banned by Google" — ANECDOTE-DRIVEN, WEAKLY REPRESENTATIVE. This traces to a few Trustpilot reviews of koala.sh (TrustScore ~2.6, only ~16 total reviews — a tiny sample). The vivid quotes ("30+ websites all banned," "banned 1-2 months after publishing") come from a very small number of distinct reviewers and are repeated verbatim across secondary articles. The harshest write-ups (eesel.ai, aidetectplus.com) are competitors selling alternative tools (clear conflict of interest). No documented Google manual action / independent verification of full-site bans attributable to Koala specifically; some "ban" reports are entangled with billing/account-ban disputes. SearchLogistics' broader claim is that AI-spam sites lost rankings in Google's March 2024 update — a general AI-content risk, not a Koala-specific full-site-ban phenomenon.

Has Koala improved / representativeness: Koala now markets GPT-5/Claude 4, real-time SERP analysis and deep research mode (it has iterated), and makes no anti-AI-detection claims; multiple independent reviewers say Koala content CAN rank when edited with E-E-A-T, contradicting an "every site gets banned" narrative. Net: both talking points are based on real but cherry-picked/competitor-amplified evidence and overstate representativeness — neither is a robust, Koala-specific liability. Hence uncertain, leaning toward "these soft spots are weak/not clearly representative."

verifications.claim: KoalaWriter (Koala AI) has no built-in plagiarism/duplicate/uniqueness checker, no plagiarism-detection module, and no independent fact-checking module — its only verification-adjacent capability is Deep Research / real-time-data web fetching that augments generation and cites sources.
verifications.evidence:
Verified against Koala's own first-party sources; initial third-party review claims of a "built-in plagiarism checker" were contradicted by official docs and are treated as affiliate-marketing inaccuracy.

1) PLAGIARISM/DEDUP/UNIQUENESS — CONFIRMED ABSENT. Koala's official FAQ "Is the output plagiarism-free?" (support.koala.sh) does NOT describe any built-in checker; instead it presumes the user runs their OWN external plagiarism tool and helps interpret it: "Please check the plagiarism results to see which parts were flagged as plagiarized. Usually, we find that these were commonly used phrases [because plagiarism checkers are sensitive]." It only asserts output quality ("rest assured that the KoalaWriter articles are plagiarism-free"), not a feature. The full FAQ index (16 articles) has no plagiarism-checker/uniqueness/dedup/fact-check article. The official pricing page (koala.sh/pricing) and homepage (koala.sh) list features (SEO optimization, internal linking, real-time data, AI images, Amazon affiliate, rewriting, outline editor, publishing integrations, Deep Research, schema, bulk) with NO plagiarism/dedup/uniqueness/fact-check module. The full official changelog (koala.sh/changelog) shows NO release of plagiarism detection, uniqueness checking, deduplication, duplicate-content detection, or an independent fact-verification module across all feature categories.

2) FACT-CHECK — CONFIRMED it is only Deep Research / real-time web data, not an independent verifier. The official Real-Time Data feature page (koala.sh/features/real-time-data) describes only web augmentation: "The AI performs targeted searches to gather current information," current data "incorporated into your content," optional source citation, and "cross-referenced from multiple sources when possible" — i.e., sourcing during generation, not a downstream fact-verification module that audits the generated claims. Koala and third parties alike still advise manual human fact-checking.

Caveats/nuance (do not weaken the verdict): (a) Koala markets a separate paid AI-detection-bypass product "Koala Secure" / "Koala Bypass" — that is anti-AI-detection rewriting, NOT plagiarism/dedup/fact-check. (b) A "Rewrite Captions" option exists for YouTube-to-blog articles to avoid copying transcripts verbatim — a narrow rewrite toggle, not a corpus dedup/plagiarism scanner. (c) Some third-party SEO/affiliate reviews loosely claim a "built-in plagiarism checker," but this is directly contradicted by Koala's own FAQ telling users to run external checkers; multiple other reviews and Koala's docs agree there is NO built-in plagiarism checker. Net: the differentiation position holds.

verifications.claim: SEO.ai's real current pricing is Single Site $149/mo and Multi Site $299/mo (25% off annual; free trial), and the much lower tiers quoted by review blogs (PikaSEO $39/$79; Hastewire $29/$79/$199) are unreliable/wrong — so competitive price comparisons must use the live official seo.ai/pricing page, not the blogs.
verifications.evidence:
Primary source — the official seo.ai/pricing page — confirms the current prices EXACTLY as claimed: Single Site $149/mo, Multi Site $299/mo (up to 3 websites or languages), "Save 25% with annual payment," monthly plans no binding period, prices ex-VAT, and a free trial via "Get started for free." The page slug is "Pricing-Jul-2025," consistent with a current (2025+) page.

The third-party low prices are demonstrably unreliable and mutually contradictory for the SAME product: PikaSEO's "SEO.ai Review 2026" (Updated Feb 2026) states SEO.ai = Basic $39 / Pro $79 with NO mention of $149, $299, Single Site, or Multi Site, citing only "independent research." Hastewire's "SEO.AI Review" states a different structure entirely: Starter $29 / Pro $79 / Enterprise $199. Two reviews of the same tool disagree on both plan names and amounts — a hallmark of AI-generated/fabricated review pricing rather than real quotes.

Crucially, SEO.ai's OWN archived pricing page (seo.ai/pricing-old2) shows yet another distinct historical structure: Basic $49 / Plus $149 / Enterprise $749 (annual = "2 months free"). This proves SEO.ai has revised pricing multiple times (the existence of /pricing-old2 and /pricing-teammate supports the "old price" hypothesis). None of the blog figures ($39/$79 or $29/$79/$199) match either the current official prices OR this documented legacy structure — so they correspond to no real SEO.ai tier, current or archived.

The claim's actionable conclusion — verify against the live official page, distrust the blog low-prices — is solidly confirmed. Two caveats that do NOT undermine the core claim: (1) the specific "$1 / 7-day trial" detail is NOT confirmed on the official page, which only says "Get started for free" with no $1 or 7-day specifics; (2) the exact attribution mechanism (confusion with same-named SEOWriting.AI) is plausible but unproven — SEOWriting.AI's own tiers are ~$19/$79, which also do not precisely match the blog numbers, so the low prices look more like fabricated/outdated review content than a clean SEOWriting.AI mix-up.

verifications.claim: SEO.ai's Trustpilot rating is disputed: one source shows 3.5/5 with 19 reviews, another (an interested SEO/AI-content blog) claims 4.2/5 with 78% recommending. A direct Trustpilot check is needed to establish the true score, review count, and positive/negative split.
verifications.evidence: Direct verification against Trustpilot's own page (https://www.trustpilot.com/review/seo.ai), read via stealth browser since WebFetch was 403-blocked. Trustpilot's embedded JSON-LD structured data is authoritative and gives: aggregateRating ratingValue "3.5", reviewCount "19". The official ratings-distribution dataset (also Trustpilot JSON-LD): 5-star = 11 (58%), 4-star = 0 (0%), 3-star = 1 (5%), 2-star = 0 (0%), 1-star = 7 (37%), total 19. So the REAL numbers are 3.5/5, 19 reviews, positive (4-5 star) = 11/19 = 58%, negative (1-2 star) = 7/19 = 37%, one neutral. This CONFIRMS the claim's 3.5/5 + 19-review figure as the true live value, and REFUTES the competing 4.2/5 + 78% figure: that figure traces to hastewire.com (Hastewire, a third-party AI-writing/AI-detection platform — a commercial, non-neutral source, not a neutral reviewer and not SEO.ai itself), and its 78%-recommend number does not match Trustpilot's actual 58% positive share. The claim's central thesis — the two cited numbers conflict, the high one comes from an interested party, and a direct Trustpilot check is required — is therefore substantiated. One nuance: the claim labels the high-figure source an 'SEO marketing blog'; it is more precisely a commercial AI-content vendor's blog (Hastewire), still interested/non-neutral but not the SEO.ai vendor. Additional finding strengthening the polarization point: the distribution is bimodal (58% five-star vs 37% one-star, near-zero in between); the most recent 1-star review explicitly alleges the 5-star reviews may be inauthentic, and one 5-star review is authored by 'Oskar Mortensen' — a name that appears as a named SEO.ai support agent in two separate 1-star complaints, indicating at least one 5-star review was likely written by SEO.ai staff. Net: trust the 3.5/5 (19 reviews, 58% positive / 37% negative); the 4.2/5-78% claim is unsupported by primary data.

Read the Trustpilot profile (seo.ai, Anguilla-based, UNCLAIMED, 19 reviews, TrustScore 3.5; distribution 58% 5-star / 37% 1-star) directly from the DOM via stealth browser (WebFetch was 403-blocked). And didn't answer my emails -- I had to contact my debit card to ask them to block their attempts." SYSTEMATIC EVIDENCE = 4 DISTINCT Trustpilot reviewers across 3 different years and multiple countries reporting the same cluster (charge at/after trial or while subscribed + cancellation not honored/impossible + support emails ignored/undeliverable): (1) Phil US 2026 [the $149x3 case]; (2) Michael US Oct-2024 — subscribed customer invoiced $149 while support unresponsive, threatened FTC/ITA complaint; (3) Digital Bug SK Apr-2024 — "never asked us about charging... charged 3 months in row... can not stop it. verifications.claim: Surfer SEO end-to-end auto-publish to WordPress/any CMS requires Scale+ ($219/mo) or an API add-on; API calls consume Content Editor credits; API rate limit is 5 req/s.
verifications.evidence:
Mixed result — directional thrust holds but the cited specifics are partly wrong/unverifiable, so the claim as written cannot be confirmed.

CONFIRMED parts (first-party): (1) API access is gated to the top tier(s). Surfer's API Introduction doc states verbatim: "This feature is available with the Peace of Mind or Enterprise plan." (2) API usage consumes plan credits: same doc says "All API requests you send will consume actual limits from your account and count toward your plan's quota," and the API Troubleshooting doc shows Content-Editor POSTs returning 422 "Quota exceeded" — i.e. each Content Editor created via API burns a Content Editor credit, exactly as in the UI.

REFUTED / OUTDATED parts: (a) There is no "Scale" plan and no $219/mo tier on the current pricing page. Live tiers are Discovery $49, Standard $99, Pro $182, Peace of Mind $299, and Enterprise (custom). API access is listed only on Peace of Mind ($299) and Enterprise — so the gate is $299, not $219. The "$219 Scale" and the standalone "$29 API add-on" figures survive only in third-party/cached blog summaries; the first-party KB articles for "API Add-on Purchase" and "Add-ons and Extra Limits" now return 404, consistent with a plan restructuring that folded API into Peace of Mind. (b) "End-to-end auto-publish" is not a native Surfer capability at any tier. WordPress integration is included on ALL plans (even $49 Discovery) but it is an optimize/import-export integration, not an API-driven publisher. The Surfer API itself does NOT publish to a CMS: per the API Examples doc it only returns "a clean HTML version of your Content Editor draft," and notes "WordPress and Shopify accept strings with HTML tags as 'content'" — meaning YOU must build the CMS push via the WordPress/Shopify REST API yourself. So true end-to-end auto-publish requires the gated API ($299+) PLUS custom integration work.

UNVERIFIABLE part: the "5 req/s" rate limit was NOT found in any first-party Surfer doc fetched. First-party docs disclose only an endpoint-specific limit (AI Detector = 60 requests/min). The "5 requests/second" figure appears only in third-party blog summaries (e.g. eesel/affinco), not on docs.surferseo.com, so it is unconfirmed.

Net for the differentiation premise: a competitor genuinely cannot get programmatic publishing on a cheap Surfer plan — it needs the $299 Peace of Mind tier (or Enterprise), API calls burn Content Editor credits, and even then Surfer returns HTML only (no native CMS auto-publish), so "low-price end-to-end publishing" remains a real differentiation angle. But because the claim's concrete facts ($219 Scale tier, 5 req/s, framing of native auto-publish) are outdated/incorrect/unverified, the verdict is uncertain rather than confirmed.

verifications.evidence:
证伪。该"隐藏成本"在 Frase 当前(2026)架构下已不存在——$35/月 的独立 SEO/Writing add-on 已被并入所有套餐,无需额外购买。证据链清晰解释了评测间的"矛盾":这是新旧两套定价架构造成的陈旧信息错配。

(1) 官方定价页 frase.io/pricing(第一手,最强证据):明确写 "Every plan — including Starter — gives you full access to the Frase AI Agent, SEO and GEO content optimization." 当前套餐为 Starter $49 / Professional $129 / Scale $299 / Enterprise(定制)。页面上不存在任何独立的 "SEO Pro" 或 "unlimited AI writing" 功能型 add-on;仅有"用量型"附加项(更多 articles / audit pages / visibility prompts)与额外席位 +$29/seat。SEO+GEO 优化、AI Agent、AI 写作均为各套餐内置功能而非付费 add-on。

(2) 描述 $35/月 SEO add-on 的来源是过时的:demandsage.com 评测原文称 "if you're willing to unlock some more powerful features, you will have to pay $35/month extra",但它用的是【旧套餐名】Solo $15 / Basic $45 / Team $115,且文章原始发布日期为 2025-05-12(schema metadata)。即该 $35 add-on 属于 2026 前的旧架构。

(3) 当前评测交叉印证并直接点破矛盾来源:aiflowreview.com(注明 "As of May 2026")列出与官网一致的 Starter/Professional/Scale 阵容,并明确警告:"If you still see plan names like Solo, Basic, or Team on other sites, you're likely looking at stale information." —— 而带 $35 add-on 的评测正是用 Solo/Basic/Team 命名。

补充:help.frase.io 的定价/add-on 帮助文档旧 URL 现已 404(站点随定价改版重构),而搜索引擎缓存快照仍返回旧价(Basic $45/Team $115),这正是题面所担心的"官网 vs 近月评测可能矛盾"的成因——属陈旧索引,而非现行政策。结论:旧 $35 SEO add-on 已并入套餐/取消,该隐藏成本在现行架构下不复存在。判 refuted(高置信,基于第一手定价页 + 2026-05 现行评测互证)。

verifications.claim: Frase 的 AI writer 引用造假是系统性软肋(非 dailyaireviews 单次个案):其测出的「11 条引用、5 条外链张冠李戴(如 Ahrefs 链接指向竞品 ranklytics.ai)」应可被 1-2 个独立 hands-on 复测复现。
verifications.evidence:
默认怀疑、尽力证伪后,结论分两层:

(1) 针对「外链张冠李戴」这一【具体失效模式】——未找到任何第二方 hands-on 复测。dailyaireviews(原始来源,已核实细节:单篇「AI 写产品描述」文章测了 11 条内联链接,其中 5 条外链目标 URL 与所标注来源不符——「Ahrefs May 2025 study」实际指向竞品 ranklytics.ai、CMI 指向 uschamber.com、两条 Linearloop 均指向 airops.com、一条捏造的「内部测试」指向无关 YouTube;4 条 dailyaireviews 内链准确、1 条 Printful 外链真实但略夸大)是【唯一】真正点开逐条验证 Frase 自动插入引用链接的测评。我核查的其他 4 篇独立 hands-on 评测(searchendurance、originality.ai、eesel.ai、autoposting.ai)【全部未测】引用/外链/来源准确性——它们只笼统说输出「generic / repetitive / 需人工编辑 / 含 AI 痕迹」。故「张冠李戴」这条精确发现目前仍只立足于单次测试,无法判 confirmed。

(2) 针对「引用造假是否系统性」这一【更宽命题】——证据偏向「系统性」:(a) 独立的 Frase 专属信号:G2 用户评测报告 Frase「sometimes hallucinates or uses outdated data」「accuracy of real-time statistics is lacking」,这是 dailyaireviews 之外对 Frase 输出不准确的独立佐证,但属泛化的幻觉/过时数据,而非精确的「链接指向错误目标」模式;(b) 类目级证据充分:大量研究显示 AI writer 系统性捏造/错配引用与链接(Tow Center/Columbia 测 8 大 AI 搜索引擎 >50% 引用错误、Gemini/Grok 过半引用指向死链;多项学术研究 AI 引用捏造率约 25%–50%)。dailyaireviews 观察到的失效正是该文献预测的典型表现,且与「Frase 有原文访问权时引用准确、需外引权威时 URL 频繁不匹配」的机理一致。

净判:不是孤立偶发(类目层面系统性成立、且有 Frase 专属 G2 佐证其输出不准),但「Frase 外链张冠李戴」这一具体发现未被任何第二个 hands-on 测试独立复现,故定 uncertain——倾向「AI writer 类目通病、Frase 大概率不能幸免」,但缺乏针对 Frase 该失效模式的第二方直接复测。

verifications.claim: Jasper official pricing: Pro $59/mo (annual) & $69/mo (monthly) single seat; Business is custom with a 12-month minimum commitment; the official pricing page currently shows only Pro/Business; and Creator $39 may have been stopped for new users.
verifications.evidence:
First-party verification against the live jasper.ai/pricing page (fetched 3x, 2026-06-07) confirms the load-bearing numbers: Pro = $69/mo per seat (monthly) / $59/mo per seat (annual, "Save ~20%"), 1 seat included; monthly Pro = cancel anytime, annual Pro = 12-month term. Business = "custom pricing" with the page stating verbatim "Business plans are customized to your needs and begin with a 12 month commitment." The official page displays ONLY Pro and Business tiers — no Creator/Starter/Teams tier appears in any fetch. So the three falsifiable first-party assertions (Pro prices, Business 12-mo minimum, page shows only Pro/Business) are CONFIRMED exactly.

CAVEAT on the Creator sub-point (the claim itself hedged this, and correctly so): the claim's speculation that "Creator $39 is stopped for new users" is NOT supported by first-party evidence and is contradicted by recent third-party sources. Creator is indeed absent from the official pricing page, but the *reason* is unverifiable from the page alone. Demandsage (last updated 2026-06-05) and several other 2026 reviews still list Creator as an active plan for new users at $39/mo annual / $49/mo monthly, and explicitly attribute the "no longer available for new users" language to the older *Starter* plan, not Creator. Conclusion: Creator's absence from the page is real, but "discontinued for new users" remains uncertain/likely-overstated — Jasper may simply be sales-gating or A/B-hiding it. Net: confirmed for the verifiable first-party facts; the Creator-deprecation guess stays unconfirmed.

verifications.claim: Jasper Business 实际成交价区间约 $250–350/月起(第三方/用户报告),官方不公示,需向 sales 询价或找近12个月真实合同/报价佐证。
verifications.evidence:
两部分分别核验,结论:"官方不公示"为真,但"$250–350/月起"的具体价格带被更可靠的真实合同数据证伪。

(1) 官方不公示——CONFIRMED。Jasper 官方定价页(jasper.ai/pricing)对 Business 档只显示 "custom pricing" + "Contact Sales",并注明 "12 month commitment";唯一公示价是 Pro 档 $69/月(月付)/$59/月(年付,含1席)。所以"不公示、需询价、有12个月起约"属实。

(2) $250–350/月起——REFUTED(证据不足且被真实数据反驳)。该数字只出现在二手测评博客的转述里(如 hyperwriteai / socialrails 写"reportedly starts at $250+/month"),属无来源估算、互相抄录;遍寻未找到任何第一手买家报告(Reddit/论坛/具名合同)印证 $250–350/月。相反,两家公布"匿名真实合同/成交数据"的采购平台口径都明显更高:
 - Vendr(45 笔真实采购):年度合同中位数 $25,000(约 $2,083/月),区间 $7,000–$68,820/年(绝对下限约 $583/月)。
 - SpendHound(去标识真实合同):SMB(50–1,000 人)均值 $5,934/年(约 $494/月,33 家);Enterprise 均值 $44,532/年(25 家),且声明"actual pricing, not published rates or estimates"。
即便取最低口径(SpendHound 的 SMB 均值 ~$494/月、Vendr 的合同下限 ~$583/月)也都高于 $350,故"$250–350/月起"的价格带不成立。方向性判断("真实价远高于 $59 Pro、必须询价")是对的,但本论断的核心——具体美元区间——被证伪。建议改述为:真实成交多在 ~$500–$2,000+/月(年化 ~$6k–$25k 中位,Enterprise 可达 $45k+/年),且为 custom/询价制。

verifications.claim: Jasper has no native one-click WordPress publishing and no first-party WordPress connector in its integration marketplace; pushing content to WordPress still relies on copy/paste, the browser extension, or Zapier/Make/n8n automation.
verifications.evidence:
PRIMARY SOURCE (Jasper's own integrations page, jasper.ai/integrations): the official first-party integration list contains 16 connectors — Slack, Google Drive, Microsoft SharePoint, Adobe Workfront, Semrush, Box, Salesforce, Google BigQuery, Webflow, Microsoft Word Add-In, Google Sheets, Google Docs, Google Chrome, Zapier, Make, and Pabbly Connect. Notably it includes Webflow (a native CMS connector) but NO WordPress connector. So Jasper itself ships a first-party CMS integration for Webflow but deliberately not for WordPress.

CONNECTION METHOD CONFIRMED: WordPress is reachable only via middleware — Zapier (zapier.com/apps/wordpress/integrations/jasper confirms the connection is made *through* Zapier, with no native Jasper-WP path), plus Make (make.com/en/integrations/jasper-ai/wordpress), n8n (n8n.io), Albato, and Pabbly. The Jasper Everywhere Chrome extension works inside the WP block editor as an in-field writing overlay, but that is an authoring assist, not an automated/native publish connector.

NO OFFICIAL PLUGIN: searches of the WordPress.org plugin directory surfaced no Jasper-authored official plugin; third-party 'AI for WordPress' roundups dated 2026 explicitly state Jasper 'relies on browser extensions or third-party automation tools rather than native WordPress plugins' and contrast it with Surfer SEO / Bertha AI, which DO ship native WP plugins.

CONCLUSION: I adversarially looked for a recently-launched first-party WP plugin or one-click publish and found none. The claim that Jasper still has no native one-click WordPress publish and no first-party WP connector (relying on copy/paste, the extension, or Zapier/Make/n8n) holds as of June 2026. Minor nuance: the browser extension does operate inside the WP editor, so it is marginally more than pure copy/paste, but it is not a native publishing integration and does not refute the claim.

competitors.oneLiner: Semrush ContentShake AI (now rebranded "Content Toolkit" inside the Semrush platform) is an SEO-data-fed AI writer that pulls keyword/competitor data from Semrush's database to draft and optimize blog articles in one guided workflow, positioned as "the go-to resource for small teams with big content goals."
competitors.targetCustomer: Small marketing teams, solopreneurs, bloggers, and SMB content marketers — especially existing Semrush customers who want SEO-informed drafts without leaving the ecosystem. Paid scenario: people who value Semrush's keyword/SERP data integration over raw writing quality and will pay a premium for the "research + write + optimize + publish" bundle. It explicitly markets against ChatGPT, Jasper, Copy.ai, and Surfer SEO, leaning on its proprietary SEO data as the wedge.
differentiators: Native access to Semrush's SEO database — topic/keyword suggestions with real search volume, keyword difficulty, and search intent baked into the brief
All-in-one guided workflow: content ideas to brief to AI draft to real-time SEO/readability/tone scoring to image generation to publish, in one tool
'Brand Voice' feature: train tone from a ~200-word sample, up to ~50 brand voices on the paid plan
Marketing proof-claim that AI content can rank: 'We analyzed 20K blog articles, surveyed 700+ Semrush users, and interviewed industry experts'
Tight integration with the broader Semrush suite (keyword/audience/competitor data) for users already on the platform
One-click WordPress publishing via official plugin + Google Docs export

features.publishing: Yes — two paths. (1) One-click publish to WordPress via the official 'Semrush Content Toolkit / ContentShake' plugin (carries over formatting, headings, images; supports categories & tags). (2) Export/Send to Google Docs. BUT the WordPress plugin is weak: ~2,000+ active installs, rated only 2.6/5 on WordPress.org with repeated 1-star reviews about connection failures ('reinstalled 2 or 3 times and would not connect', 'constantly says We are aware of the issue; please try later', 'doesn't integrate with my site'). No automated dedup/uniqueness pipeline and no humanization layer beyond Brand Voice.
integrations: Deep integration with the Semrush platform/Content Toolkit (keyword, audience, competitor data)

First-party: Semrush's official ContentShake/Content Toolkit feature overview (KB 1358) and Pricing & Limits page (KB 1536) enumerate the COMPLETE feature set and plan quotas, and NEITHER lists any plagiarism checker, AI-content detector, originality check, or uniqueness/dedup feature. verifications.claim: SEOmatic has no fact-checking, plagiarism-detection, AI-detection, or automated dedup/uniqueness quality-control module — it relies only on dynamic variables/spin syntax + Content Score + human review.
verifications.evidence: Adversarial check across SEOmatic's official homepage, pricing, features, vs-Byword comparison, and duplicate-content blogs, plus 3rd-party reviews. SEOmatic's official 18-item features list contains NO fact-check, plagiarism, AI-detection, or duplicate-detection/uniqueness-checker module. The only QC-adjacent items are: (1) "Spin Syntax" (verbatim: "Use spin syntax to easily create different versions of your content, making sure each piece is unique and avoiding repeated text") — a generation-side variation mechanism, not a detector/measurer; (2) "Content Score" (homepage: "Score each client's page against the SERP and AI answers") — SERP/AI optimization scoring, not fact-check/plagiarism/dedup; (3) brand-voice "humanization" tone training. Pricing tiers ($149/$399/$899) list none of the four QC modules; the lone "QA & internal review" mention describes the MANUAL workflow SEOmatic replaces. SEOmatic's duplicate-content articles only give manual advice (avoid over-templating, enrich datasets), no built-in dedup tool. 3rd-party reviews confirm "SEOmatic... does not replace the human editing step" and note occasional content "inaccuracies." Contrast: competitor Surfer SEO explicitly names "Plagiarism Checker" + "AI Detector & Humanizer" — features SEOmatic never lists. CAVEATS lowering certainty from absolute: SEOmatic has no public API docs / sparse Help Center (undocumented in-app behavior possible); and the attack must be framed precisely as "no fact-check / no plagiarism / no AI-detection / no automated dedup-verification," since Spin Syntax could be loosely marketed as "uniqueness." One browser-automation attempt was discarded as contaminated by stale tabs (served Byword/Surfer, not SEOmatic; the two are confirmed separate competitors, no rebrand) — all confirmation rests on fresh WebFetch of genuine seomatic.ai URLs + WebSearch.

verifications.claim: SEOmatic (seomatic.ai) publishes to WordPress fully plugin-free via the built-in REST API + Application Passwords, AND it offers no rollback after publishing.
verifications.evidence: Verdict splits by sub-claim. SUB-CLAIM A (plugin-free via REST API + Application Password) = CONFIRMED first-party. SEOmatic's own WordPress integration page states verbatim in its FAQ: "Do I need to install a WordPress plugin? No. SEOmatic connects directly to WordPress via the built-in REST API using application passwords. No plugin installation required," plus "No plugin needed — connects in under 5 minutes" and "Direct API connection — no plugin to install or maintain." The connect-WordPress doc describes the one-click Application Password approval flow; requirements are self-hosted WordPress 5.6+, HTTPS, and REST API enabled (security plugins like Wordfence that disable REST API must be turned off). This is unambiguous and from the vendor. SUB-CLAIM B ("no rollback after publishing") = UNCERTAIN / unproven, though circumstantially supported. I found NO rollback/revert/version-history/restore-previous-version feature anywhere across the official site, all feature pages, the changelog (feedback.seomatic.ai), or the indexed help-center article titles (Getting Started, How-To Guides, FAQ, Troubleshooting, Features: Drag&Drop, Generative AI, Schema, Meta Tags, Dynamic Update). SEOmatic's only post-publish capabilities are FORWARD operations: "republish to update existing content" and "Dynamic Update," which OVERWRITES pages when source data changes (the Dynamic Update page explicitly has no version-history/revert mention) — the opposite of rollback. Because it publishes via the WordPress REST API, any undo would rely on WordPress's own revisions or manual deletion in the CMS, not a SEOmatic feature (a search result noted deletion "may need to be done directly in your CMS rather than through SEOmatic"). BUT I could not get a first-party affirmative "there is no rollback": every docs.seomatic.ai URL returns 404 to both WebFetch and a live rendered browser, so I could not read the full FAQ/Troubleshooting body text to rule out a buried revert/delete article. Absence of a documented rollback feature is strong but not conclusive. NOTE: do not conflate the competitor seomatic.ai with the unrelated nystudio107 "SEOmatic" Craft CMS plugin (seomatic.io / GitHub) that surfaces in searches. NET FOR OUR NARRATIVE: the plugin-free REST API + Application Password mechanism is solid and citable; the "no rollback" differentiator is defensible (no rollback feature is advertised or documented) but should be framed as "SEOmatic provides no rollback/version-restore feature; published changes are forward-only overwrites" rather than an absolute "rollback is impossible," since we lack an explicit vendor denial.
